solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: City hospital that has its own church

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a district rather than a plain noun

parts.note: the French capital
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A city hospital proudly boasting a chapel of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the district served by a single church and its clergy, so it is the area that has its own church.

clue.text: Pan lid upside-down

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word upside-down means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a top

explanation.surface: A saucepan lid flipped over on the hob.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot is a cooking vessel, much like a pan.

clue.text: Search odd magazine at back of store

parts.note: rum is a British word for strange or odd
mag is the short form of magazine

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of store

explanation.surface: Hunting for an unusual magazine at the rear of a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' looks like it might pick alternate letters, but it is a synonym: rum, as in a rum business.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search untidily by turning things over.

clue.text: Filming celebrities' heavenly bodies

parts.note: shooting a film is filming it
celebrities are stars

explanation.surface: Filming the gorgeous physiques of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly bodies' suggests attractive film stars, but it means objects in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting stars are meteors, bright streaks in the night sky, so they are celestial objects.

clue.text: Small clubs turn and move around display

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs
to roll is to turn over and over

explanation.surface: A bridge player's instruction: play small clubs, then rotate the table display.
explanation.definitionFit: To scroll is to slide the contents of a screen up or down, moving around what the display shows.

clue.text: Journalist, or similar

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a reporter covering a particular subject or place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Or similar' reads like 'or someone of that sort', but similar is a definition in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word names a reporter; as an adjective it means corresponding or analogous.

clue.text: Nationality of some womanisers …

indicators.note: some of the word means only part of it, a run of its letters

parts.note: letters two to six of the word

explanation.surface: Asking what country some philanderers come from, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Omani is the nationality of someone from Oman, on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: … one of whom mad aliens fancy

definitions.note: whom refers back to the womanisers of the previous clue

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Crazed extraterrestrials take a shine to one of the womanisers.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the clue before, so 'whom' means womanisers. 'Fancy' reads as a verb, to be attracted to, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a man who chases women, so he is a womaniser.

clue.text: Got together around post office for speed

indicators.note: turned around, so the word for got together is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: met means came together
PO is the standard abbreviation for post office

explanation.surface: People gathered at the post office in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it wants one piece placed round another, but here it only turns the first word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or pace of something, especially music, so it is a synonym of speed.

clue.text: Legendary woman Mike and I dream about

parts.note: Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved round about, scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mike and the speaker both dream of a woman out of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid is a mythical sea creature, half woman and half fish, so a woman of legend.

clue.text: A lot of people like neck hair?

definitions.note: the many, as a noun for most people
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ..., the bulk of people
second meaning: a jokey adjective from mane, the long hair on a horse's neck, said the same way

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: a horse's mane is its neck hair, and something like a mane would be mane-y, which sounds the same. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The many means the majority of people, while mane-y would describe something resembling a horse's flowing neck hair.

clue.text: Wingless biting insects in meadow

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two ends, so without them only the inner letters remain

parts.note: fleas are small biting insects

explanation.surface: Fleas that cannot fly, biting away out in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleas really are wingless, so the word reads as a true description; here it means FLEAS loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic or old word for an open grassy field, a meadow or pasture.

clue.text: Support is overdue to pass laws

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
taken as written
overdue means late

explanation.surface: Backing for a bill is long delayed in getting through parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make or enact laws, the job of a parliament.

clue.text: Moroccan and Argentine dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Moroccan and an Argentinian dancing together, perhaps a tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' looks like a second nationality alongside Moroccan, but it is just the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tangerine is a native of Tangier, the Moroccan port city, so is a Moroccan.

clue.text: Politicians mostly acknowledge Poles

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to greet someone is to acknowledge them
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Politicians largely recognising Polish people, perhaps on a diplomatic visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it means the two magnetic poles, north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greens are members of environmentalist political parties, so the word names a group of politicians.

clue.text: Head of Euro Millions bagging £25 in Peterlee?

indicators.note: bagging means putting something in a bag, so one piece is wrapped around another
the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of Euro
M is the abbreviation for million or millions
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: A lottery win of twenty-five pounds on EuroMillions, the big European draw, for someone in a County Durham town.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterlee is a new town in County Durham named after the miners' leader Peter Lee; his name inside the town's name is an eponym, and the question mark flags this example.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym is the person a place or thing is named after, and Peter Lee's name is there in Peterlee.

clue.text: A peaceful state, Iran somehow restricting vehicle for transporting goods

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so one set of letters holds the other inside
somehow says the letters arrive in some other unstated order

parts.note: taken as written
a van is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: A calm nation, yet Iran is somehow limiting freight lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A peaceful state' looks like a country, encouraged by Iran next to it, but it is a state of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana, in Buddhism, is a state of perfect peace and freedom from desire.

clue.text: Rear female deer

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a female red deer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a verb, a deer rearing up, but it is the adjective for back.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means at the back; as a noun it is the female of the red deer.

clue.text: Meeting involving church's withdrawal

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a session is a meeting of a council or court
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A synod meeting at which the church announces it is pulling out.
explanation.walkthrough: The church sits after the second letter of the meeting word. The 's stands for 'has', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Secession is the formal act of withdrawing from a union, federation or organisation.

clue.text: Funny man caught Greek character ignoring Ron

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: omicron is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian caught a Greek figure snubbing someone called Ron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ron' looks like a man's name but is the last three letters to remove from the Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a comedian, a professional funny man.

clue.text: Called wanting golf organised

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: rang means called on the phone
Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G

explanation.surface: Someone phoned, keen to get a round of golf set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting golf' reads as a wish to play, but it means the G is missing from the phone word.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an event or business is to organise or manage it, so ran fits organised.

clue.text: Provide weapons for group, and safety equipment

parts.note: to arm is to supply with weapons
a band is a group of people

explanation.surface: Kit a squad out with guns and protective gear.
explanation.definitionFit: An armband is an inflatable float worn on the arm by a learner swimmer, a piece of safety kit.

clue.text: Regularly envy Andrew's escape

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone routinely jealous of Andrew's getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape or avoid something, so the verb is a synonym of escape.

clue.text: Consume flesh, but start to be shunned

indicators.note: the start of a word being shunned means its opening letter is avoided and dropped

parts.note: meat is animal flesh as food

explanation.surface: A diet rule: eat meat, but avoid starters.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat food is to consume it.

clue.text: Pardon former copper before Senate evacuated

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: evacuated means emptied, so the inside letters go and only the outer two remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of Senate

explanation.surface: A retired policeman is pardoned before the Senate building is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is slang for a police officer, the surface reading; the wordplay wants the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to forgive or pardon their fault.

clue.text: Auditor's immediately in crisis

indicators.note: an auditor is literally a listener, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: straight away means immediately

explanation.surface: An accountant reports at once that the firm is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking books, but it means a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait, usually as straits, is a position of difficulty or distress, as in dire straits.
